patch.value: Static contribution manifest: persist the install-time contribution inventory so the command registry is built from data and extension modules import only when a contribution is actually invoked

The data required to gate activation precisely is already computed and then thrown away. 'pm extension --install' loads and activates the extension and reports registered_actions (src/sdk/extension.ts:2310, commandSummary.action_paths) - in the sandbox repro it printed registered_actions: ["my-ext-ping"]. The install record it writes, .agents/pm/extensions/.managed-extensions.json, persists only the coarse capabilities[] array and the manifest entry. Every subsequent invocation therefore re-derives contribution knowledge the installer already had, and because capabilities[] is the only surviving signal, the runtime must fall back to the conservative and global tiers that force eager import (see pm-j0w7j9).

The declarative authoring form does not help either, and it is worth being precise about why. composeExtension(blueprint) / ExtensionBlueprint (pm-8mxg, pm-lfdv) already describe every surface an extension contributes - renderers record, parsers record, preflights, services, hooks.afterCommand, itemTypes, itemFields, searchProviders. But the blueprint is a value inside the module, so learning it costs exactly the import the gate is trying to avoid. pm has a complete declarative description of contributions and no cheap channel to read it through.

Proposal - separate the contribution inventory from the contribution implementation, the pattern VS Code settled on with contributes + activation events:

1. Extend the manifest (and/or the .managed-extensions.json install snapshot) with a typed contributions block: command paths, renderer targets keyed by command, hook phases with optional command scope, parser targets, preflight targets, declared item types and fields.
2. Derive it mechanically at install time from the already-loaded blueprint or activation result, so authors do not hand-maintain it and it cannot drift from the code. Hand-authoring stays possible for extensions that want to declare ahead of a build step.
3. Build the command registry, --help surface, unknown-command suggestions, and type/field schema from that inventory alone. Import a module only when one of its contributions is actually reached.
4. Verify the snapshot against the module at install/update time and on version change; treat a mismatch as an install-time failure, not a runtime surprise.

This retires the capability-tier heuristic entirely rather than tuning it: with a precise per-contribution inventory there is no need for GLOBAL_ or CONSERVATIVE_ tiers, and the schema-vs-activation.commands tension pm-halx had to decide by fiat disappears because a schema contribution names the types it registers.

Second-order wins: extension-contributed commands become visible in --help and in unknown-command suggestions without paying activation; pm-qfdd's commander-singleton leak shrinks because dynamic registration moves to data; contracts/MCP surfaces can enumerate extension commands statically.

Extension discovery resolves every contributed command path, renderer target, hook phase, parser target, and item type without importing any extension module; a workspace with N installed extensions shows no per-extension cost on commands that invoke none of their contributions

author: harness:claude-code
message: Typed lineage: supersedes the manifest-gated activation approach, builds on declarative blueprint work, unblocks commander-singleton and SDK-first goals
